text: The game no longer uses the old six-sided-die battle rules, but most tests still run on them. Remove them?
context: About 1,000 lines of code and many tests pin the map to the old rules. Removing them simplifies the code, but a future era could use them.

options.label: Keep the old rules for now, and move the tests that should follow the real game to the current dice
options.rationale: Tests then check what players play; deleting code can follow later.

options.label: Remove them completely
options.rationale: Simplest code, most test work, and no old-rules option for other eras.

options.label: Leave everything as it is
options.rationale: No cost, but the cruft and wrong-rules tests remain.

text: Should the player's download carry the historical notes and source lists?
context: Nothing shows them on screen. They are about 11 KB of the compressed scenario download. The text stays in the project either way.

options.label: Leave them out of the player's download
options.rationale: Smaller download; the notes stay in the source for us.

options.label: Keep them and show them in the game
options.rationale: Makes use of the writing, but needs new screens.

text: Popular resistance goes. What about barricades, the smaller defence bonus for any side holding a city?
context: They are separate rules. Without popular resistance, barricades (-1 to the attacker's roll) is the only city defence left.

options.label: Keep barricades as they are
options.rationale: Cities stay a little harder to take, the same for everyone.

options.label: Remove both
options.rationale: Simplest, but cities lose all defence value.

options.label: Make barricades stronger to replace popular resistance
options.rationale: Keeps the old balance, but the bonus then applies to all factions.

text: Should the battle sheet show why a unit's strength is what it is (men, morale), not just the total?
context: The game does not record this per unit today, so showing it needs a small change to what each battle saves.

options.label: Yes, show men and morale per unit
options.rationale: Players can see why a unit counted for less; small engine change.

options.label: No, total strength only
options.rationale: No engine change, but less explanation.

text: What should the casualty counter count?
context: The game records battle losses and frostbite. Units that surrender or are disbanded don't record their men yet.

options.label: All men lost: battles, surrenders, disbanded units and cold
options.rationale: Matches what players expect from casualties; needs men added to surrender records.

options.label: Battle losses only
options.rationale: Simplest, but a surrendered army counts as no loss.

options.label: Battle losses and surrenders only
options.rationale: Leaves out cold losses, which are small.
